translations.text: The word of the Lord came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, concerning what he saw about Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen, all you peoples, and let the earth and all its inhabitants pay attention. Let the Lord God be a witness among you, the Lord from his holy temple.
For behold, he will leave his place, come down, and arrive upon the high places of the earth.
The mountains will shake beneath him, and the valleys will melt like wax before fire and like water flowing downhill.
All this is because of Jacob’s wicked deeds and the sins of the house of Israel. Now, what is Jacob’s wickedness but Samaria? And what is the sin of the house of Judah but Jerusalem?
I will make Samaria like a fruit-guard’s shelter in a field and a place for planting a vineyard. I will cast her stones into a ravine and lay bare her foundations.

They will smash all her carved images and burn all her statues with fire, and I will bring all her idols to destruction. For she collected them from the wages of prostitution and amassed them from the wages of prostitution.
Therefore he will mourn and lament and go naked and barefoot. He will mourn like dragons and grieve like the daughters of sirens.
For her wounds have grown severe, because they have reached Judah and come near the gates of my people and Jerusalem.
You who are in Gath, do not boast; and you who are in Accarim, do not renew mockery from the house. Put dust on your heads because of your mockery.
Did not she who dwelt in prosperity come out of her cities? Inhabitants of Shinar, mourn over the house that is near her; it will take from you the painful blows.
Who began good things for the one dwelling amid pain? For evils came down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem.
The rattle of chariots and the thunder of horses, you inhabitant of Lachish! She led the daughter of Zion into sin, for Israel’s wicked deeds were found in you.
Therefore she will give those who are sent away as far as the inheritance of Gath. Empty houses became useless to the kings of Israel.
They will bring as far as your heirs, you inhabitants of Lachish; as an inheritance, the glory of the daughter of Zion will reach Adullam.
Shave yourself and cut off your hair for your tender children. Make your baldness wide like an eagle’s, for they have been taken captive from you.
They began devising troubles and doing evil on their beds, and at dawn, in the light, they carried out those same things, because they did not lift their hands to God.
They coveted fields and seized orphans and took houses by force. They seized a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
Therefore the Lord says this: Behold, I am planning evils against this people, from which you will not lift your necks, and you will not walk upright, because the time is evil.

On that day I will take up a proverb against you. They will lament aloud and say, “We have become utterly miserable! The portion of my people was measured with a line, and there was no one to prevent him from turning it back. Our fields were divided.”
Therefore there will be no one to assign a portion by measuring line and lot in the assembly of the Lord.
Do not weep with tears, and let them not shed tears over these things, for he will not remove the disgrace.
The one who said that the house of Israel angered the Spirit of the Lord—if these are his ways, his words are not good with him, and my people have not walked uprightly before me.
It opposed its own peace in hostility. They will strip off its skin to take away hope, the devastation of war.
Therefore the leaders of my people will fall from their luxurious homes. Because of their evil ways they were driven out. Draw near to the everlasting mountains.
Stand up and go, for there is no rest for you here. Because of uncleanness you were utterly destroyed; you were driven away without anyone pursuing you.
A lying spirit arose and dripped wine and drunkenness upon you, and it will be from the dripping of this people.

Jacob will surely be gathered together with everyone, and he will surely receive the remnant of Israel. I will bring them back together, like sheep in distress, like a flock in the midst of its fold. They will be driven by people through a breach.
For they made a breach before them, passed through the gate, and went out through it. Their king also went out before them, and the Lord will lead them.
And he will say: Hear, ruler of the house of Jacob and remnant of the house of Israel! Is it not for you to know justice?
You hate what is good and seek what is evil; you strip their skin from them and their flesh from their bones.
Just as they ate the flesh of my people, flayed their skin from them, crushed their bones, and tore their flesh apart as though for cauldrons, and their meat as though for pots,
so they will cry out to the Lord, and he will not hear them. He will turn his face away from them at that time, because they tormented them through their deeds.

This is what the Lord says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray: They bite with their teeth and proclaim peace to him, but if nothing is put into their mouths, they stir up war against him.
Therefore you will have night instead of vision, and darkness instead of divination. The sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
The dream-seers will be ashamed, and the diviners will become a laughingstock. Everyone will revile them, for there will be no one who listens to them.
But I am filled with the Spirit, with the Lord’s strength, with justice and power, to tell Jacob of his ungodliness and Israel of his sins.
Hear this, leaders of the house of Jacob and remnant of the house of Israel, who despise justice and twist everything that is right,
who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with injustice.

Its leaders judged for bribes, its priests gave answers for payment, and its prophets pronounced divinations for silver. Yet they took refuge in the Lord and said: Is not the Lord among us? No evil will come upon us.
Therefore, because of you, Zion will become plowland, Jerusalem will become like a fruit-keeper’s hut, and the mountain of the temple will become a forest grove.
In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be clearly visible, established on the summits of the mountains. It will rise above the hills, and many peoples will hurry to it.

Many nations will go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob. They will show us his ways, and we will walk in his paths. For laws will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

He will judge among many peoples and rebuke mighty nations, even those far away. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take up a sword against nation, nor will they learn to wage war anymore.
Each person will rest under their own vine and under their own fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten them, for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken this.
Even if all peoples walk, each in their own ways, we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
On that day, says the Lord, I will gather those who are broken, and I will welcome those driven away and those whom they rejected.
I will make the broken one into a line of descendants and the crushed one into a mighty nation, and the Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on forever.
And you, tower of the flock, dark daughter of Zion: the former dominion of the kingdom will come upon you and enter, from Babylon to the daughter of Jerusalem.
And now, why have you experienced evil? Did you not have a king, or has your counsel perished, so that your labor pains have grown strong like those of a woman giving birth?

Labor, grow strong, and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth. For now you will leave the city, and I will settle you in the open country. You will reach Babylon, and from there he will rescue you; from there the Lord your God will deliver you from the hands of your enemies.
And now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “Come, let us trample her, and let our eyes look upon Zion.”
But they did not know the Lord’s plan or understand his will, for he gathered them like sheaves on a threshing floor.

Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. You will crush many peoples and shatter nations with them, and you will offer their wealth to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
Now the daughter will be besieged within an enclosure, for he has brought distress upon you. With a rod they will strike the cheeks of the tribes of Israel.

And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are small among the thousands of Judah. From you will come forth for me one who is to be ruler of Israel, whose origins are from the beginning, from the earliest days of the world.
Therefore he will give them up until the time when the woman in labor gives birth, and the remainder of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.

He will stand and watch and shepherd his flock with the strength of the Lord and in the glory of the name of the Lord their God. They will be established, for now he will become great to the ends of the earth.
And there will be peace for him. When the Assyrian comes into your land and reaches your country, he will raise up against him seven shepherds and eight rulers of men.
They will shepherd the Assyrian with the sword, and the land of Nimrod within its moat. He will rescue you from the Assyrian when he comes into your land and reaches your borders.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the Gentiles, in the midst of many nations, like dew fallen from the Lord and like a drop upon the grass, so that it may not be gathered, and not one [?], and may not remain among the sons of men.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the Gentiles, in the midst of many nations, like a lion among the animals of the forest and like a young lion among flocks of sheep: when it passes through, it tears them apart and seizes them, and there is no one to rescue them.
May your hand be raised over your oppressors, and may all your enemies be destroyed.
On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots.
And I will destroy the cities of your land and remove all your strongholds. I will remove all your sorceries from your hands, and there will be no diviners among you.
I will wipe out your carved images and your pillars from your midst, and you will no longer bow down to the works of your hands.
I will cut down your groves from your midst and destroy your cities.
In anger and wrath I will take vengeance among the nations because they did not listen.
Listen to what the Lord said: Rise and plead your case with the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Hear the Lord’s case, you hills, you valleys, and you foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against his people, and he will bring charges against Israel.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I grieved you, or how have I oppressed you? Give me an answer.
For I brought you up from the land of the Egyptians and redeemed you from the house of slavery, and I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam before you.

My people, remember what Balak king of the Moabites planned against you, and what answer Balaam son of Beor gave him, from the allotments to Gilgal, so that the righteousness of the Lord may be known.
With what shall I come before the Lord and take refuge in my exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings and year-old calves?
Will the Lord accept thousands of rams or tens of thousands of fat goats? Shall I give my firstborn for my wickedness, the fruit of my body for the sins of my soul?
You have been told, O human, what is good and what the Lord asks of you: only to do justice, to love mercy, and to be ready to walk after the Lord your God.
The Lord’s voice will call out over the city, and he will save those who fear his name. Hear, O nation: who will put the city in order, if not fire?
and the house of the lawless man who stores up lawless treasures, and with the arrogance of injustice
And can the lawless man be justified by scales and a bag of deceitful weights?
Thus they filled their houses with ungodliness, and its inhabitants spoke injustice, and their tongues boasted in their mouths.
And I struck you with destruction because of your sins.
You will eat but not be satisfied. I have rejected you, and you will be seized and will not escape. Whoever escapes will be handed over to the sword.
You will sow but not reap. You will press out oil but not anoint yourself with oil, and wine but not drink wine.

And the lawless people of my people will be destroyed, along with all the works of the house of Ahab. You followed their counsels, so that I will hand you over to destruction and your inhabitants to hissing, and you will bear the reproach of the peoples.
Woe to me, for I became like one gleaning ears at harvest and like one gathering the grapes left after the vintage, and there was no cluster of the first harvest from which I could eat.
Woe to my soul, for the God-fearing person has perished from the earth, and there is no upright person among humanity. They all contend with bloodshed; each grievously oppresses his neighbor.
They prepare their hands for evil. The ruler makes demands, and the judge speaks words of peace according to the desire of his own soul.

And I will take away their good things like a moth that eats and moves along a measuring rod. On the day of visitation, woe, woe! Your punishments have come and arrived; now there will be weeping for them.
Do not trust friends, and do not put your hope in rulers. Be careful about telling anything to the one who shares your bed.
For a son dishonors his father, and a daughter will rise against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and a man's enemies are the members of his own household.
But I will look to the Lord; I will wait for God my Savior, and the Lord my God will hear me.
Do not trample on me, my enemy, for though I have fallen, I will stand again. Even if I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light.
I will endure the Lord's anger, for I have sinned against him, until he vindicates my case and grants me justice. He will bring me out into the light, and I will see his righteousness.
My enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me, “Where is the Lord your God?” My eyes will look upon her; now she will be trampled like mud in the road.
A day of plastering bricks and of your obliteration will that day be; that day will cast aside your rights.
Your cities will come under siege and be plundered by the Assyrians, and your fortified cities will be divided into portions, from Tyre to the River, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
And the land will be destroyed, together with its inhabitants, because of the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with the staff of your tribes, and the flock of your inheritance, who dwell alone in the forest in the midst of Carmel. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the days of your departure from the land of the Egyptians, I will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their strength. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
They will lick the dust like snakes that crawl along the earth. They will be troubled in their confinement, and they will tremble before the Lord our God and be afraid of you.
Who is God like you, who takes away lawlessness and overlooks the injustices of the remnant of the land of his inheritance? He does not retain his anger as a testimony, because he delights in mercy.
He will return and have compassion on us, and he will submerge our sins and cast all our lawless deeds into the depths of the sea.
He will give faithfulness to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as he swore to our fathers in days of old.
